instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a sieve under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes. No peeking.
Pull the small tough side muscle off each scallop if it's still there. Pat the scallops very dry with paper towels, transfer them to a bowl and toss with the 1/2 tsp salt.
Meanwhile, cut the bell peppers into thin strips and mince the 6 garlic cloves. Cut 3 of the scallions into 2 inch pieces, keeping the white and green parts apart. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk the broth, oyster sauce, wine and sugar. In a cup, stir the cornstarch into 3 tbsp cold water until smooth.

Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat for 1 minute. Add 1 tbsp of the oil and half the scallops in a single layer. Leave them alone for 1 minute, until golden underneath. Flip them and cook for 30 seconds. Transfer them to a plate. Wipe the pan, add 1 tbsp oil and cook the rest the same way. They'll finish cooking in the sauce.
Turn the heat to medium-high and add the last 1 tbsp oil, the bell peppers and the scallion whites. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the peppers are bright and just tender.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant and hasn't browned.
Stir the sauce and pour it in. Bring it to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir the cornstarch mix again and pour it into the middle of the pan, stirring, until the sauce turns glossy and thick, about 30 seconds.
Return the scallops and any juices from the plate. Cook for 1 minute, turning them in the sauce. Cut the biggest one in half: it's done when it's opaque all the way through.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the scallion greens and the chopped cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version with 20 or more ratings turned up, so this leads with Food.com's Garlic Scallops, the closest readable version of this exact dish. It builds a sauce of broth, oyster sauce, wine and sugar around garlic and red bell pepper and thickens it with cornstarch. It simmers the scallops in the sauce for 5 minutes, which would toughen them, so here they're seared first, set aside and returned for the last minute, the way Healthy World Cuisine's bay scallop stir-fry does it. Quantities are scaled up by a quarter, with a second pepper and an extra clove of garlic. The 30 minutes includes the rice.
